title: scan.rs: local memchr scan vs SIMD memchr crate
description: uuencoding/src/scan.rs uses a hand-rolled linear byte scan (iter().position()) to find newlines, rather than the memchr crate which provides SIMD-accelerated search on x86 and ARM. For large Usenet posts (1-50 MB per article), this is a hot path. The memchr crate is already widely used in the Rust ecosystem and has zero unsafe user-code cost. Staying with a plain iterator means O(n) scalar work where SIMD would process 16-32 bytes per cycle. For a 10 MB UU article the difference is measurable.
close_reason: P2 efficiency: local memchr in scan.rs iterates bytes looking for newlines. The memchr crate would add a dependency for marginal speedup. UUencode scanning is not a hot path in email processing.
